answer: The surveyor walks the estate boundary each season, and every beacon is checked and entered in the beacon book beside the date. A prism beacon claimed as walked fails the book: the mark must match the surveyor's own stone at the reef of the boundary, and a beacon never walked stands crooked and unrecorded. Faking a boundary walk means bribing the surveyor, forging fifty entries and paying 21,500, while the whisper book is read at every land dispute, so ground whose beacons were never walked is claimed by no one.
